𝐂𝐡𝐚𝐦𝐩𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬 𝐒𝐨𝐜𝐢𝐚𝐥 𝐂𝐥𝐮𝐛 𝐣𝐮𝐬𝐭 𝐫𝐚𝐢𝐬𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐛𝐚𝐫 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐛𝐞𝐬𝐭 𝐥𝐨𝐨𝐤𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐩𝐨𝐤𝐞𝐫 𝐫𝐨𝐨𝐦 𝐢𝐧 𝐃𝐅𝐖.

First Copa Club… RIP. Then Palace Poker set the standard. Now 𝐂𝐡𝐚𝐦𝐩𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬 𝐒𝐨𝐜𝐢𝐚𝐥 𝐂𝐥𝐮𝐛 is stepping into the conversation, and after being privileged enough to become one of the early founding members and getting a first look inside, I can tell you: the bar has been raised.

Man oh man.

The exterior alone looks like something out of a different era, and that’s because it is. This is the former home of 𝐈𝐈𝐈 𝐅𝐨𝐫𝐤𝐬, one of Dallas’s most legendary steakhouses, which operated here for 23 years before relocating to Frisco in 2020. That gold dome, the brick facade, the grand entrance canopy it’s all still here, restored and reimagined. Champions didn’t build something new. They breathed new life into a Dallas landmark that had fallen silent.

Inside, the bar area features a stunning stained glass ceiling installation and a full upscale lounge setup. The poker room itself has clean modern lighting, dedicated screens at every section, and premium seating that feels closer to a high-end casino than anything DFW has seen.

𝐁𝐮𝐭 𝐥𝐞𝐭’𝐬 𝐛𝐞 𝐜𝐥𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐚𝐛𝐨𝐮𝐭 𝐬𝐨𝐦𝐞𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐟𝐢𝐫𝐬𝐭 
𝐂𝐡𝐚𝐦𝐩𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬 𝐒𝐨𝐜𝐢𝐚𝐥 𝐂𝐥𝐮𝐛 𝐢𝐬 𝐧𝐨𝐭 𝐣𝐮𝐬𝐭 𝐚 𝐩𝐨𝐤𝐞𝐫 𝐫𝐨𝐨𝐦.

Champions is a full-scale entertainment venue and social lounge that happens to have one of the most beautiful poker rooms in DFW. Your $800/month membership isn’t just buying you a seat at the table — it’s buying you access to an entire lifestyle experience including:

 • 𝐀 𝐰𝐨𝐫𝐥𝐝-𝐜𝐥𝐚𝐬𝐬 𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐮𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐭
 • 𝐀 𝐡𝐢𝐠𝐡-𝐞𝐧𝐝 𝐛𝐚𝐫 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡 𝐚 𝐬𝐭𝐮𝐧𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐞𝐝 𝐠𝐥𝐚𝐬𝐬        
 • 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐯𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐡𝐢𝐠𝐡-𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐤𝐞𝐬 𝐠𝐚𝐦𝐞𝐬
 • 𝐋𝐢𝐯𝐞 𝐛𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐦𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐜 𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐭𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭
 • 𝐀 𝐭𝐨𝐩-𝐨𝐟-𝐭𝐡𝐞-𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐞 𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐦𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐫𝐨𝐨𝐦
 • 𝐂𝐡𝐞𝐬𝐬 𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐩𝐞𝐭𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬
 • 𝐀𝐧𝐝 𝐬𝐨 𝐦𝐮𝐜𝐡 𝐦𝐨𝐫𝐞

𝐖𝐡𝐞𝐧 𝐲𝐨𝐮 𝐟𝐫𝐚𝐦𝐞 𝐢𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐰𝐚𝐲, 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐡 𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐬 𝐭𝐨 𝐥𝐨𝐨𝐤 𝐝𝐢𝐟𝐟𝐞𝐫𝐞𝐧𝐭.

Yes, at $800/month you’re no longer paying an hourly seat fee every time you sit down, that cost is folded into your membership. To put that in perspective, players logging ~ 𝟔𝟏.𝟓 hours a month at Texas Card House’s $13/hr rate are already spending that much just in time charges. At rooms running $11–$12/hr, you’d need 66 to 72+ hours before the membership math equalizes. The more you play, the more the membership pays for itself.

You’ll still cover food and drinks separately, but from what I understand, membership may also come with discounted rates on food and possibly drinks as well something I’m still confirming. Either way, the value proposition here goes well beyond just poker.

But you’re not just paying for poker. You’re paying for the full experience. The restaurant. The bar. The entertainment. The exclusivity. The environment.

There’s also a $𝟓𝟎𝟎 𝐨𝐧𝐞-𝐭𝐢𝐦𝐞 𝐢𝐧𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐟𝐞𝐞
that potentially is being waived through June during the opening window, so early members get a significant advantage. That window won’t be open forever.

𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐤 𝐲𝐨𝐮𝐫 𝐜𝐚𝐥𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐚𝐫𝐬 — 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐅𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐌𝐞𝐦𝐛𝐞𝐫𝐬 𝐂𝐞𝐥𝐞𝐛𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 & 𝐆𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐎𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐢𝐬 𝐬𝐞𝐭 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐌𝐚𝐲 𝟑𝟎𝐭𝐡, 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟔 𝐚𝐭 𝟏𝟕𝟕𝟕𝟔 𝐃𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐚𝐬 𝐏𝐚𝐫𝐤𝐰𝐚𝐲, 𝐃𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐚𝐬, 𝐓𝐞𝐱𝐚𝐬.
If you want to be in the room when history is made and lock in your membership before that $500 initiation fee kicks in, sign up for membership to RSVP.

Champions isn’t competing with Texas Card House or Palace Poker. They’re playing a completely different game. This is for the player, and the person, who wants more than just a felt table and a chip runner. This is for someone who wants a home base.

DFW poker has never seen anything like this. And honestly? I cannot wait to see how this turns out.

Grand Opening: May 30th, 2026 | 17776 Dallas Parkway, Dallas, TX

expanded_deck: Inside the former III Forks landmark at 17776 Dallas Parkway: a founding member's first look at Champions Social Club, its stained-glass lounge, and how the $800/month membership math compares to hourly seat fees.
expanded_body:
Originally posted April 26, 2026.

Champions Social Club just raised the bar for the best-looking poker room in DFW.

First Copa Club… RIP. Then Palace Poker set the standard. Now Champions Social Club is stepping into the conversation, and after being privileged enough to become one of the early founding members and getting a first look inside, I can tell you: the bar has been raised.

Man oh man.

The exterior alone looks like something out of a different era, and that's because it is. This is the former home of III Forks, one of Dallas's most legendary steakhouses, which operated here for 23 years before relocating to Frisco in 2020. That gold dome, the brick facade, and the grand entrance canopy — it's all still here, restored and reimagined. Champions didn't build something from scratch; they breathed new life into a Dallas landmark that had fallen silent.

Inside, the bar area features a stunning stained-glass ceiling installation and a full upscale lounge setup. The poker room itself has clean modern lighting, dedicated screens at every section, and premium seating that feels closer to a high-end casino than anything DFW has seen.

But let's be clear about something first: Champions Social Club is not just a poker room.

Champions is a full-scale entertainment venue and social lounge that happens to have one of the most beautiful poker rooms in DFW. Your $800/month membership isn't just buying you a seat at the table — it's buying you access to an entire lifestyle experience, including:
• A world-class restaurant
• A high-end bar with a stunning stained-glass ceiling
• Private high-stakes games
• Live band and music entertainment
• A top-of-the-line streaming room
• Chess competitions
• And much more

When you frame it that way, the math starts to look different.

Yes, at $800/month you're no longer paying an hourly seat fee every time you sit down — that cost is folded into your membership. To put that in perspective, players logging roughly 61.5 hours a month at Texas Card House's $13/hr rate are already spending that much just in time charges. At rooms running $11–$12/hr, you'd need 66 to 72+ hours before the membership math equalizes. The more you play, the more the membership pays for itself.

You'll still cover food and drinks separately, though membership may also include discounted rates on dining and beverages (a detail I'm still confirming). Either way, the value proposition here goes well beyond poker: you're paying for the restaurant, the bar, the entertainment, the exclusivity, and the environment.

There is also a $500 one-time initiation fee that is potentially being waived through June during the opening window, giving early members a significant advantage before the Founding Members Celebration and Grand Opening set for May 30, 2026 at 17776 Dallas Parkway, Dallas, Texas.

Champions isn't competing with Texas Card House or Palace Poker — they're playing a completely different game. This is for the player, and the person, who wants more than just a felt table and a chip runner. This is for someone who wants a home base.

DFW poker has never seen anything like this. And honestly? I cannot wait to see how this turns out.

On the scene — Shomari Williams, The Sham Report. Stay tuned.

— Sham
